newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index breaches 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index breaches 1996 high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.5 percent to breach last year's high by the start of play on Wednesday.
The index climbed to 308.90, breaking through its 1996 high of 308.77. It began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
Day-on-day, Latin America climbed 2.1 percent to 580.14, Asia fell 0.6 percent to 258.05, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.4 percent at 141.80.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.83 percent day-on-day at 168.45 at 1000 GMT, after breaching 1996's 165.948 high on January 9.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.28 percent at 497.217, calculated after the close of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It touched a high last year of 505.452 on July 4, and recorded its 458.369 low on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, slipped 0.01 percent to 125.78 by the start of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.23 percent at 103.95, Asia fell 0.17 to 132.49 and East Europe was flat at 162.36. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
